title: Symphony No. 4 in E minor
hook: An autumn symphony that ends in tragedy, built on a tune borrowed from Bach.

painting.title: Isle of the Dead (third version)
painting.pairingNote: Painted two years before the symphony, with the same grave stillness and the same refusal of a consoling ending.

facts: Brahms’s last symphony, written in the summers of 1884 and 1885 in the Austrian Alps. He conducted the premiere on 25 October 1885 in Meiningen.
The finale is a [[passacaglia|passacaglia]]: thirty short variations over an eight-bar theme adapted from a Bach cantata. It was an old Baroque form, used here for a Romantic tragedy.
Unusually for a symphony of its time, it ends in the minor key, without consolation.
The opening theme is built from a chain of falling thirds, an interval pattern that returns at the very end.
bigPicture.inOneLine: resignation (I), a noble procession (II), rough high spirits (III), fate (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: No introduction: the symphony begins in mid-sigh. A [[sonata-form|sonata form]] movement that starts in gentle melancholy and ends in catastrophe.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: violins in pairs of notes, falling then rising, like breathing out and in.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a proud, rhythmic call in the woodwinds, followed by a broad, ardent melody for cellos and horns.

stops.hear: Violins sigh in two-note phrases; woodwinds echo each one a moment later
stops.happening: Theme 1. The notes trace a chain of falling thirds

stops.hear: A sharp, fanfare-like rhythm in the winds; then cellos and horns sing a wide, passionate melody
stops.happening: Theme 2

stops.hear: Hushed, mysterious string ripples with soft fanfares in the woodwinds
stops.happening: A moment of suspended time before the close of the [[exposition|exposition]]

stops.hear: The opening sighs return exactly, then turn somewhere new
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] begins by pretending to be a repeat

stops.hear: The opening notes, stretched out very slowly in the woodwinds, with quiet string ripples between them
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]] steals in. You may not notice you are home until the sighs resume at normal speed

stops.hear: The sighing theme, now fortissimo, with the basses chasing the violins
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. The gentle theme has become furious, in [[canon|canon]]

stops.label: Last bars
stops.hear: Pounding timpani
stops.happening: A tragic close

notice: The slow-motion return at ≈ 7:10 is one of Brahms’s subtlest strokes. Rewind and hear it twice.

movements.heading: Andante moderato
movements.summary: A slow movement with an antique flavour, opening with horns alone. Its second theme is among the warmest things Brahms wrote.

stops.hear: Horns alone, in a solemn, archaic-sounding call
stops.happening: The opening uses an old church scale, which gives it its distant, legendary colour

stops.hear: Clarinets take the tune over plucked strings
stops.happening: Theme 1, like a slow procession with [[pizzicato|pizzicato]] footsteps

stops.hear: Cellos sing a broad, glowing melody; violins decorate above
stops.happening: Theme 2

stops.hear: The procession returns, more agitated, rising to a stern climax
stops.happening: The middle of the movement

stops.hear: The glowing melody again, now in the full, rich string section
stops.happening: The emotional summit. The strings are divided into many parts for extra warmth

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The horn call returns
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

movements.heading: Allegro giocoso
movements.summary: The loudest, most boisterous movement Brahms put in a symphony, complete with a triangle. A burst of rough humour before the tragedy.

stops.hear: The full orchestra crashes in; a triangle jingles
stops.happening: Theme 1. Piccolo, contrabassoon and triangle join the orchestra for this movement

stops.hear: A gentler, graceful tune in the violins
stops.happening: Theme 2

stops.hear: The pace drops; horns and woodwinds play softly, as from a distance
stops.happening: A brief quiet episode

stops.hear: The opening bursts back
stops.happening: The return, and a stamping close

movements.heading: Allegro energico e passionato
movements.summary: Eight chords, then thirty [[variation|variation]]s on them, without pause. The theme is always there, sometimes on top, sometimes buried in the bass.

stops.hear: Eight stern chords in winds and brass, climbing step by step
stops.happening: The theme. Trombones play for the first time in the symphony

stops.hear: Plucked strings and drums; then a stiff woodwind tune
stops.happening: The first variations. The eight notes move into the bass

stops.hear: The strings take over with a sweeping, passionate melody
stops.happening: The variations grow more lyrical and more urgent

stops.hear: The pulse slows. A solo flute, alone and halting
stops.happening: The flute variation. The loneliest moment in the symphony

stops.hear: Trombones and horns in soft, hymn-like chords
stops.happening: A [[chorale|chorale]] in E major. A brief vision of peace

stops.hear: The eight chords crash back as at the start
stops.happening: The second half begins. The dream is over

stops.hear: Variations of growing violence: stabbing accents, rushing scales
stops.happening: The drive to the end

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Woodwinds and strings answer each other in falling pairs of notes
stops.happening: The chain of falling thirds from the first movement returns

stops.hear: The tempo quickens
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. It ends in E minor, unreconciled

notice: Try to hear the eight rising notes in every variation. Once you can follow them, the movement becomes a single unbroken line.

threads.title: Falling thirds
threads.body: The interval pattern of the very first theme returns in the final variations.

threads.title: Old forms, new feeling
threads.body: A church scale in the second movement and a Baroque passacaglia in the finale.

threads.title: No consolation
threads.body: The symphony begins and ends in E minor.
